title: Model Release Compatibility SLA: Prompt, Parameter, and Output Stability Manifest
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a formal, machine-readable compatibility SLA for locked model releases that covers: (1) canonical prompt/IO schema and supported parameter aliases, (2) output stability guarantees and semantic-difference thresholds, and (3) published performance profiles (latency percentiles, token throughput, memory, and backend variant mappings). The goal is to give customers deterministic expectations when they pin a model version and for the platform to automatically gate upgrades and rollouts by these contracts.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable release contract (JSON Schema v1) is produced and stored in model-catalog under /manifests/{model}:{version}/compatibility.json

Contract contains: prompt schema, allowed parameter aliases, deprecated-parameter mapping, canonical example I/O, output-stability spec (semantic similarity floor and token-diff thresholds), and performance profile with p50/p95/p99 latency under defined workloads.
Runtime enforces contract at onboarding: incompatibility prevents auto-promotion to
Regression harness runs on each candidate release and returns a pass/fail score. Passing threshold documented in the manifest and surfaced to PM/owner.
Publish tooling to generate a human-readable Compatibility SLA page (Console) and a programmatic endpoint for partner automation.
At least one internal model has been onboarded using the new contract and used in a canary rollout with fallback mapping configured.
implementation_notes: Define canonical prompt schema: name, required/optional slots, types (string, enum, structured JSON), size limits, canonical examples. Use flexible field-level 'aliases' mapping (e.g., max_tokens -> tokens_max) to support client-side parameter drift.

Output stability: two-tier checks — structural conformity (shape + required fields) and semantic fidelity (embedding-based similarity >= 0.92 for core answers, with token-diff tolerances for boilerplate). Compute both deterministic checksum and semantic hash to detect noisy regressions.

Performance profile artifact: standard JSON keys {p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_sec,peak_gpu_mem_mb,quantized_variant}. Include workload descriptor used for measurement (seq_length, batch_pattern, prompt_mix).

Onboarding flow: generate contract during model import; run baseline ephemeral evaluation on standard promptset (open-source + customer-provided). Produce report and attach to manifest. Failures create a blocker in Linear with links.

Compatibility gating: implement a 'compat-check' task in runtime and console ingest pipeline. If semantic or structural regression occurs beyond thresholds, block auto-rollout and mark release 'Compat-Blocked'.
Backwards compatible parameter evolution: support 'soft-deprecations' with mapping rules and deprecation windows communicated via manifest and Console notifications.

Publishing: write compatibility.json and performance.json to S3 model-catalog; notify Console service and update model index. Provide REST endpoint /models/{id}/releases/{v}/compatibility and a signed URL for artifact download.
Telemetry: emit metric compat.check.failure{model,version,check_type} and latency histograms for contract evaluation. Hook to alerts for repeated regressions.
Security: ensure artifacts land in customer partition for private releases and KMS-encrypt manifests for Private deployments.
test_plan: Automated regression suite: run on every candidate build — structural + semantic checks. Embed sampling to detect nondeterministic outputs.
Prompt-fuzzing: mutate canonical prompts (whitespace, param aliasing, reordering) and assert canonical responses remain within semantic threshold.
Throughput & latency bench: simulate production batch patterns (small interactive vs bulk embedding) and verify performance profile matches published numbers within 10%.
Canary A/B: route 1% traffic to canary model, compare metrics and QoS signals; automated rollback if compat failures or user-facing regressions detected.
E2E acceptance: create PRD + runbook and validate manual sign-off from PM and Reliability owner before GA.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec and schema review (owner + API + SDK teams). Merge compatibility.json schema into model-catalog repo.
Phase 1: Implement contract generator in onboarding pipeline and run for one internal model as a pilot.
Phase 2: Add runtime compat-check enforcement and Console surface. Start canary rollouts with fallback map to previous compatible version.
Phase 3: Gradual increase to GA for new public model imports and require manifest for pinned versions in the Console UI.
Fallback: automatic routing policy to previous pinned variant on 'Compat-Blocked' status and incident runbook activation.

notes_for_pm: We need PM to prioritize acceptance of the default thresholds (semantic floor and token-diff tolerances) and to coordinate with Sales/Support on customer communication templates for deprecations and blocked upgrades. Also request a product decision on whether performance profile variance of +/-10% is acceptable for GA.
additional_context: This charter complements existing pinned-version manifests but focuses on deterministic contracts that enable automated gating and observable guarantees. The intent is both developer UX (predictable pin behavior) and operational safety (automated rollback and alerts).
